subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Broken Windows Theory
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Broken Windows Theory.

hook.text: A clean alley stays clean. Spraypaint one wall and within weeks the whole alley is covered in graffiti and litter.

buildup.text: Wilson and Kelling proposed that visible disorder signals that nobody cares, which invites more disorder.

discovery.text: Keizer tested this in the Netherlands. People littered twice as often near a graffitied wall than near a clean one.

twist.text: Critics argue the theory was misapplied to justify aggressive policing. The environmental signal is real; the policy.

climax.text: Small signals of disorder shape behavior. Maintaining visible order is a low-cost way to sustain social norms.

punchline.text: One broken window is permission for the next.

quiz.question: What did Keizer's experiment in the Netherlands find?
options: People littered equally regardless of surroundings
People littered twice as often near a graffitied wall
Graffiti reduced crime in the neighborhood

details.summary: The broken windows theory suggests that visible signs of disorder like vandalism and litter encourage more disorder and crime because they signal that norms of care and compliance have broken down in that environment.
details.whyItMatters: In economics, broken windows theory applies to institutional trust. When people perceive that others are cheating on taxes, cutting corners, or violating norms, compliance drops further, creating a downward spiral of norm erosion.
takeaways: Visible disorder signals that social norms are not being enforced
Small violations encourage larger violations through norm cascade
Maintaining visible order helps sustain broader compliance and cooperation

faq.question: How does broken windows theory apply to the economy?
faq.answer: When tax evasion is visibly common, more people evade taxes. When corporate fraud goes unpunished, more firms cut corners. Visible norm violations signal that cheating is acceptable, reducing cooperation and trust across the entire economic system.

faq.question: Is broken windows theory scientifically supported?
faq.answer: The evidence is mixed. Experiments in the Netherlands confirmed that visible disorder increases norm violations. However, the aggressive policing policies it inspired have been criticized for disproportionate enforcement against minority communities.
